segments.he: מְדָדוֹ בְּקָנֶה וְכוּ׳. כׇּל אֵלּוּ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה וְאָמְרוּ: יִמָּכֵר, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר. אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: יָנוּחוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרָכוֹת עַל רֹאשׁוֹ, כְּשֶׁהוּא מַתִּיר — מַתִּיר אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁתִיָּה, וּכְשֶׁהוּא אוֹסֵר — אוֹסֵר אֲפִילּוּ בַּהֲנָאָה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if a gentile «measured» the wine in the winepress «with a pole,» or if he cast a hornet out of the wine by means of a pole, or if he removed the foam on top of a fermenting barrel of wine, with regard to «all these» cases «there was» such «an incident, and» the Sages «said» that the wine «may be sold» to gentiles but one may not drink it. «And Rabbi Shimon deems» the wine «permitted» even for drinking. «Rav Adda bar Ahava says: May blessings rest upon Rabbi Shimon’s head,» as his reasoning is clear. «When he deems» the wine «permitted, he deems» it «permitted even with regard to drinking, and when he deems» the wine «prohibited, he deems» it «prohibited even with regard to» deriving «benefit» from it.
